name: Fort Hood
tagline: The largest active-duty armored post in the U.S., home of III Armored Corps and the 1st Cavalry Division, in Central Texas.
_note: Large Army post (Central Texas, Killeen). Name history: Fort Hood -> Fort Cavazos (May 2023) -> Fort Hood (July 2025, now honoring WWI Col. Robert B. Hood). A June 2026 House Armed Services amendment to restore the 2023 names was not law as of Sept 1, 2026 (CRS); verify the current name on future updates. Facts verified from official sources (home.army.mil/hood, Army.mil, Lendlease/Cavalry Family Housing, DeCA/AAFES, Wikipedia for corroborated headline facts). BAH MHA TX286 (Fort Hood) via the bah_rates single source of truth. Corrected 2026-11-09 from the website-page research (Base Guides/page-builder/research/hood-facts.md): housing is Cavalry Family Housing in partnership with Centinel, managed by WinnCompanies (no longer Lendlease), plus Liberty Village (~300 homes); Killeen ISD runs ALL on-post schools; official identity 'largest active-duty armored post in the U.S.'; 2026 Bell/Coryell CAD tax rates; TEA 2026 preliminary ratings. Removed unsourced claims (one of the largest installations in the world, longer tours common, being modernized, largest Exchange). Medium-confidence flags: base coords (approx), representative off-base ZIP 76542 (Killeen).

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Fort Hood is the largest active-duty armored post in the U.S. and the only post able to station and train two armored divisions. It is home to III Armored Corps, the 1st Cavalry Division and the 3d Cavalry Regiment, with many supporting units, including 1st Army Division West and the 13th Sustainment Command.

The post carried the name Fort Cavazos from 2023 to 2025. It was renamed Fort Hood on July 28, 2025, this time honoring Col. Robert B. Hood, who received the Distinguished Service Cross in World War I.

sections.title: Which Town? The Fort Hood Tax and Schools Decision

data.subtitle: Texas has no state income tax, so property tax and the school district do most of the work in your budget. Combined rates around Fort Hood run about 1.8% to 2.4% of taxable value before exemptions (our estimate from the 2026 appraisal district tables), and they change from town to town.
intro: Killeen ISD runs every school on post and was rated C (79) for 2026, preliminary; Harker Heights High, rated A, serves part of the district. Nearby districts were rated B: Copperas Cove (85), Salado (82), Temple (81) and Belton (80).

Copperas Cove ISD's tax rate rose from 0.7575 to 1.0549 per $100 after a 2025 bond, and US 190 through Copperas Cove is being widened until early 2029. On a home you live in, a $140,000 homestead exemption trims the school portion of the tax.

recommendations.advice: Killeen is about 11 minutes from Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center with no traffic, Copperas Cove 15, Harker Heights 16. Typical home in Killeen: $217,130 (Zillow, September 2026).
Belton and Salado, about 30 to 37 minutes away, had Class of 2025 graduation rates of 94.4% and 97.8%, at higher prices.
Combined rates run from about 1.84 per $100 in Harker Heights to about 2.41 in Temple (our estimates). Look up the exact address on the appraisal district record.
Cavalry Family Housing (more than 5,540 homes) and Liberty Village (about 300). Military OneSource says waits run from two weeks to 12 months depending on occupancy.

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: The Marvin Leath Visitors Welcome Center is off I-14 on T.J. Mills Blvd next to the main gate, open 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily, (254) 287-9909.
All gates use the Army's automated entry system. Visitors 18 and over need a REAL ID or an accepted alternative such as a U.S. passport or military ID, and can apply for a pass online.
Gate hours change, so call the Visitors Welcome Center before you rely on a gate.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post family housing is privatized. Cavalry Family Housing, in partnership with Centinel and managed by WinnCompanies, oversees more than 5,540 homes, and Liberty Village has about 300. The Army said in September 2025 that more than 5,000 families live on post in 12 housing areas.

Call (254) 285-2313, listed for both Cavalry Family Housing and the Army Housing Services Office; Liberty Village is 254-526-3788. Military OneSource says waits run from two weeks to 12 months depending on occupancy.

source.label: army.mil (September 2025); Military OneSource Fort Hood housing

sections.title: Schools
data: There are no DoD schools at Fort Hood. Killeen ISD runs every school on post: six elementary schools, a middle school and an early college high school that admits by application.

For 2026 (preliminary), Killeen ISD was rated C (79); Copperas Cove ISD B (85), Salado B (82), Temple B (81), Belton B (80) and Lampasas B (84). Class of 2025 graduation rates ranged from 88.4% (Killeen) to 97.8% (Salado).
Your assigned schools depend on your address, so confirm the district and high school with the School Liaison Office at (254) 288-7946.

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves. Around Fort Hood, property tax and insurance are a big part of the monthly cost of owning, so compare them by address.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
You have budgeted property tax and insurance for that exact address.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Home values around Fort Hood were flat to slightly down over the past year. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact Killeen ISD (on post) or your district early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office, (254) 288-7946, can tell you which high school serves your housing area.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment so you can be seen at Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center or network providers.

data.q: Is it Fort Hood or Fort Cavazos?
data.a: Fort Hood, since July 28, 2025, honoring Col. Robert B. Hood (World War I). It was Fort Cavazos from 2023 to 2025. A June 2026 House committee amendment to restore the 2023 names had not become law as of September 1, 2026.
III Armored Corps, the 1st Cavalry Division and the 3d Cavalry Regiment, on the largest active-duty armored post in the U.S.
Killeen, Copperas Cove and Harker Heights are closest, about 11 to 16 minutes with no traffic; Belton, Salado and Temple are 30 to 38 minutes away. Each town has its own tax rate and school district.
Fort Hood is MHA TX286. Use the calculator above for your grade.
